result.rationale: The diff adds embed.js with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, a substring-based origin check. Any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl (e.g. `http://discourse.example.co` for `http://discourse.example.com`) passes, so origin validation is flawed in newly added code, and no tests exist for it. The mechanism is verifiable directly from the diff.

judged_text: embed.js has no tests, including its security-relevant origin check: the postMessage handler's origin validation is a substring check (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) which accepts any origin that is a prefix of the discourse URL (e.g. http://discourse.example.co passes when the URL is http://discourse.example.com). The check is untested and wrong, though impact is low (iframe height only). A qunit test asserting strict origin equality would have caught this.
